n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, participants’ privacy concerns are estimated to be on average lower by –0.674 on a scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree) in the “temporary” condition compared to the “permanent” condition (“In thinking about what kind of photo to upload, I am concerned about my privacy”). We estimated this difference using an ordinary least squares regression of subjects’ privacy concerns on an indicator variable for the “temporary” condition (t(818) = –4.752, p < 0.001; n = 820). As a result, we reject the null hypothesis of no difference in privacy concerns between the “temporary” condition and the “permanent” condition. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 0.332 (95% CI [0.195, 0.469]).
